description:
FOUND s500 (Fable, 2026-09-28) by the review probes for perf round 37 (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s500/review/r500p-float.pl, out/r500p-float.{perl,base}).  PRE-EXISTING on main 209e7533.

REPRODUCER (perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl):
    printf "%.17g|%.17g|%.17g|%.17g|%.17g|%.17g\n", 1e-5, 1e-7, 1e-6, 123456789012345678, 1.23e-5, 4.94065645841247e-324;
    perl: 1.0000000000000001e-05|9.9999999999999995e-08|9.9999999999999995e-07|1.2345678901234568e+17|1.2300000000000001e-05|4.9406564584124654e-324
    PCL : 1e-05|10e-08|10e-07|1.2345678901234567e+17|1.2300000000000002e-05|4.940656458412465e-324
  `%.15g` and below are right on every row of the 66-double table (they are perl's own %.15g path, #1012); the divergence begins where the requested precision exceeds the shortest round-trip digits: PCL seems to print the SHORTEST representation (17 significant digits max, dragon4 `%flonum-to-digits`) and then pad/round it, instead of the exact decimal expansion of the double to N digits that C's printf gives.  `10e-08` shows a carry that was never normalised.
WHY IT MATTERS: `%.17g` is THE round-trip idiom (JSON encoders, Data::Dumper with $Data::Dumper::Useqq, Storable-free serializers, test suites comparing floats); a program that writes a float with it and reads it back gets a different double from PCL's output only in the last digit -- but `10e-08` is not a number at all for a strict reader.
FIX SHAPE (measure first; this is the float->text path perf round 37 (s500p) is profiling -- COORDINATE: whoever touches it owns this row too): for precision > 15 use the exact decimal expansion (SBCL's `sb-impl::flonum-to-digits` gives shortest digits; the exact expansion needs `rational` -> integer arithmetic, as perl's C printf does), or restrict the shortest-digit path to N <= 17 with correct rounding and NO carry left in the mantissa.  Probe table: every double in r500p-float.pl under %.16g %.17g %.18g %.20g %.16e %.17e %.25f, plus perl's `%.17g` of 0.1, 0.3, 1/3, 2**53+1, 5e-324, 1.7976931348623157e308.  Guard rows in Pl/t/sprintf-* (grep for the existing sprintf file).  Runtime-only => full sweep.
subject: sprintf `%.Ng` / `%.Ne` with N > 15 significant digits prints WRONG or MALFORMED text: `%.17g` of 1e-5 -> `1e-05` (perl 1.0000000000000001e-05), of 1e-7 -> `10e-08` (not even well-formed), of 123456789012345678 -> ...4567e+17 (perl ...4568e+17), of 1.23e-5 -> ...0002e-05 (perl ...0001e-05); the round-trip precision idiom (`%.17g`) is what serializers use
